grade.basis: Independent advisory estimate against levels.json after visual inspection of all eight complete-score pages. Viola 1 combines sustained upper-register treble-clef tone at Adagio fluido quarter=56 with alto/treble clef changes, chromatic figures, slurred quintuplet runs and articulated short figures in the Andante marcato quarter=80 middle. Pages 3-5 and 8 show the quicker passagework and changing registers; pages 1-2 and 6-7 establish the long-tone outer sections. The roughly four-minute whole work requires controlled soft bow and intonation plus accurate rest subdivisions; its short decorated runs and upper-register control suggest early advanced rather than a diploma requirement. Eight-part coordination has not automatically increased the individual grade; viola 2 is close. Estimate is representative pedagogical evidence, not exhaustive fingering certification.

grade.basis: Independent advisory estimate against levels.json from representative complete notation on score pages 1, 7, 10, 14, 17, 21, 24, 26 and 28, spanning opening, middle, late pattern changes and ending, with IMSLP whole-work duration context. The quarter=96 continuous sixteenth-note canonic patterns use a compact, ordinary violin register, mostly stepwise scale fragments, displaced octave-pattern starts and later flattened pitches. No advanced high-position, double-stop or specialist bow technique appears in the sampled notation. Violin 1 has the longest uninterrupted run, beginning alone and persisting to the final release: even small separate bows, relaxed repetitive fingerwork and concentration across roughly nine minutes are the main individual demands. Those stamina demands support intermediate level 2, potentially level 3 for a less experienced player, while the other parts have comparable material. Maintaining a canon against competing patterns is relevant rehearsal context but does not by itself raise the instrumental grade. Representative review supports an estimate within one level, not exhaustive note-by-note certification.
